chapter: Arranging career and the JPJ Quartet
title: Armstrong arrangements and George E. Lee: Budd learns to write
summary: Budd wrote arrangements for Armstrong's 1933 records and early charts for George E. Lee, borrowing standards' changes.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Louig Armstrong, you know, I told you about this 'Sweet Sue' and a few different other things we recorded, like 'The World on A String' and all of these different things that we recorded with Louie in '33. I did a lot of writing in there, although Zilher T. Randolph was musical
director. And with George E. Lee, oh, gee, I must have written many, many, many little arrangements. This was in my really learning days.
This was in your formative days.

That's right, because Jesse Stone was really the arranger, and I used to write -- I didn't know how to write for the piano and the banjo at that time, so what I would do was write the front line and I'd make up an original and I said, hey, you know the (Dinah) of Diana, the cat said yeah. I said just play Diana and this'll fit, you know. And I would start off writing like that.
